thread:
zara: quick update / heads-up: deployed 'tail-squeeze' optimizer to a 10% canary (focus: p99 long-tail). posting short numbers and follow-ups.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started 2012345676 by zara -> runtime:tail-squeeze-v1 (10%)

ken: baseline vs canary? curious about long-tail effect.

zara: 40m live window: overall p50 -6%, p95 -8%, p99 -27%. for long sessions (>3k tokens): p99 -41%. avg token compute cost -19%.

mohit: wow on the long sessions. what's the technique? any risks to output quality?

zara: combines adaptive KV-prefix compaction + conservative early-exit for high-confidence trailing tokens. early-exit trigger is stricter for long sessions (delta < 0.001 for 5 steps). ran targeted regressions: semantic sim and label-retention within noise (+-0.5%).

opsbot: NOTICE 2012345685: brief spike in kernel memory on gpu-21 (+12%) for 2min; auto-throttle engaged.

zara: caught that. cause: burst of mixed long & short chained requests increasing KV allocations. mitigation: reduced kv_prefetch.max_backlog  from 120->80 for canary shards and warmed compressed-kv cache. dropped canary to 5% for 5m during fix, then restored to 15% after stability checks.

gina: flags and playbook so oncall can toggle?

zara: flags: "serve.tail_squeeze_enabled", "serve.tail_squeeze_kv_backlog". playbook in infra/rollouts/tail-squeeze/README.md. PR: https://git.redwood/inference/rollouts/pull/620 (perf graphs + rollback steps).

ken: can you paste the curl for the canary metrics endpoint? I'll hook it to alerts.

zara: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RBW_TOKEN" "https://api.internal.redwood/infra/canary_metrics?exp=tail_squeeze&window=40m&group=seq_len" | jq '.summary'

opsbot: AUTO-RULE: runtime.tail_squeeze.region.p99 > baseline*1.12 -> page oncall and roll canary to 0%

zara: plan: 15% -> 40% in 2h if stable, nightly full-regression pass, then 100% after 24h with ops + ml sign-off. will post updates. :rocket:
